summary: Boris Ivanovich Klyuev was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Moscow State University. He worked at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (1952–1971), the CPSU Central Committee, MGIMO (1982–1988), and the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Boris Ivanovich Pankratov specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies after studying at the Eastern Institute. He held posts at Far Eastern Federal University, the Harvard-Yenching Institute, the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Boris Karpushkin was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (~1946–1951). He served as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1961–1974) and taught at MGIMO starting in 1974.

Boris Leonidovič Smirnov was an Indologist who studied at the S. M. Kirov Military Medical Academy (~1909–1914). He served as Director of Turkmen State Medical University (~1935–1956) and was a member of the Academy of Sciences of Turkmenistan (~1951–1967).

Linguist Boris Mikhailovich Lyapunov studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vatroslav Jagić and Filipp Fortunatov. He held posts at the University of Kharkiv, served as a professor at Odesa University (1899–1923), and became an academician at Saint Petersburg State University.

Boris Stavisky worked in Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, graduating from Saint Petersburg State University. He held positions at the Hermitage Museum, the State Museum of Oriental Art, the Kara-Tepe Archaeological Expedition, and Moscow State University (~1974–2006).

Boris Turayev was a historian and archaeologist who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Adolf Erman. He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University (later Imperial St. Petersburg University) from approximately 1896 until his death in 1920.

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, studying under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1925–1929). He held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1938).

Boris Vladimirovič Semičëv was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Culture, Peter the Great Museum, and Buryat Institute of Social Sciences.

Linguist and Central Asian specialist Boris Vladimirtsov studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Antoine Meillet and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University as Professor of Mongolian, the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, and the National Library.

Boris Vsevolodovič Miller was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist who studied at Moscow State University and the Lazarev Institute. He held posts at the State Museum of Ethnology, Moscow State University, and the Institute of Linguistics.
Bortolo Maria Bortolazzi was a 19th-century Indologist. He taught Greek at the Ginnasio Comunale di Bassano (1853–1854) and held a post at the Liceo Classico Jacopo Stellini until 1860.
Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Śrī Siṃha Shedra under Tubten Nyendrak, Khenpo Genam, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Boyd Michailovsky is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of California in 1981. He served as Directeur de recherche at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique from 1979 to 2010.
Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indology scholar who studied under Maria Byrski and is attested as a faculty member at the University of Warsaw in 2026.

Bradford Lyman Phillips specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning degrees from the University of Virginia and Harvard University. He also studied at Naropa University, with advisors and teachers including David Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, Michael Aris, and Jeffrey Hopkins.
Bradley L. Herling is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He has held posts as Assistant Director at Boston University and at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Archaeologist and Indologist Braj Basi Lal studied at the University of Allahabad and under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Historian and Tibetologist Brandon Dotson earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and his habilitation at the University of Munich. He held posts at SOAS University of London and the University of Munich.

Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Louisville under Patrick Pranke. In 2018, he served there as Project Coordinator and Senior Lecturer.
